findings.description: The new skill claims `scripts/check-agent-config.sh` runs the shell harnesses "in CI (all of them)", but no workflow in `.github/workflows/` invokes `check-agent-config.sh` or any `*.test.sh`; only the local, affected-subset `scripts/verify.sh` runs them, so agents are told a CI backstop exists that does not.
findings.body:
**The skill describes a CI harness job that doesn't exist.**

Line 8 of the new skill says:

> `scripts/check-agent-config.sh` runs `bash -n` and the shell harnesses in CI (all of them) and in `scripts/verify.sh` (the ones the change can affect).

No CI job does this:

- `.github/` contains only `CODEOWNERS`, `dependabot.yml` and `workflows/claude-code-review.yml`.
- `claude-code-review.yml` has two jobs, `claude-review` and `persist-metrics`. Neither calls `check-agent-config.sh`, `verify.sh`, `pre-push` or any `*.test.sh`.
- The only caller of the script is `scripts/verify.sh:42` (`check-agent-config.sh --affected "$base" HEAD`). That runs locally, only for the affected subset, and can be skipped.
- The `HEAD^1 HEAD -> a PR merge commit's diff (CI)` usage at `scripts/check-agent-config.sh:12` describes a call that nothing makes.

The skill then limits its own checklist to "the three classes that check cannot see". An agent reading it will assume a full harness run catches everything else. For example, a harness broken by the move to `tests/hooks/` reaches no CI gate.

Line 37's "Done when … the harness passes on macOS and in the CI job" points at the same missing job.

There are two ways to fix it:

- Add a `pull_request` workflow job that runs `bash scripts/check-agent-config.sh <base> HEAD` on `ubuntu-latest`.
- Or reword lines 8 and 37 to say that only `scripts/verify.sh` runs the harnesses (locally, the affected subset) and that CI has no harness job.

File: `.claude/skills/ci-and-agent-config/SKILL.md#L8` (new in this PR).

findings.description: The new skill says to change "the harnesses beside the hooks", but this PR moves every hook harness to `tests/hooks/`. It also names only the `.claude/README.md` hook table, not the second table in `.claude/hooks/README.md`.

The rewritten context block hardcodes `origin/main` in its `git log` and `git diff` lines, although line 67 says to take the trunk from `GIT_TRUNK` and line 70 uses `<trunk>`. The base used `<trunk>` throughout, so a repo whose trunk is not `main` now gets the wrong range.

`.env.example` still documents keys for skills this PR deletes (`obsidian-vault`, `daily-note`, `fix-sonar`, `wiz`/`fix-wiz`, `to-issues`/`to-epic`), and the adapt-to-project prune rows that would have dropped them are gone. `OBSIDIAN_*`, `SONAR_PROJECT_KEY` and `WIZ_*` now have no reader.

The README still says `.env` is "only for personal-integration skills", but this PR deletes all of them. Its only remaining in-repo reader is `pr-description`'s `TRACKER_ISSUE_PREFIX`, and `.claude/skills/README.md:46` overstates in the same way when it says the skills read "the `TRACKER_*` keys".
Step 3 still asks "which personal-integration tools are in use", but the Obsidian, Sonar and Wiz prune rows that consumed the answer were removed with those skills, so the question now feeds nothing.

This doc cites "the `find-dead-code` rule of thumb", but the PR deletes that skill and the companion-plugin note doesn't cover it. State the rule on its own (provenance outside the restore set was unverifiable).
The "Where" column names the `handoff` skill as if it ships here, but this PR deletes it. Qualify it as the companion plugin's, as `docs/adr/README.md:35` does for `domain-modeling`.

Skills that used to be vendored and reviewed in PRs are replaced by a self-updating third-party plugin, so upstream changes reach sessions that have broad pre-approved Bash permissions without review. One sentence on pinning or reviewing plugin updates would close that.

The new skill omits `disable-model-invocation: true`, which `writing-for-agents` makes the default for new skills. Its edit-triggered description plausibly meets the exception, but the PR doesn't state that reasoning.

A change to only `.claude/settings.json` never sets `harnesses=true`, yet `tests/hooks/push-gate.test.sh:219` reads that file to check the push-gate timeout against the hook's budget. Lowering that timeout therefore passes `verify.sh` unchecked.

The script and its test keep dispatch branches for `.claude/skills/setup-agent-env`, which exists neither in the base nor in the PR. The lead-tools/params branches and the `AGENT_REPO` unsets are dead code.

process_issues.description: Every Bash call failed with the sandbox error `apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/setgroups (nested userns is capability-restricted; caller must provide CAP_SYS_ADMIN): Permission denied`. That ruled out `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`/`git diff`/`git rev-parse` for the orchestrator, all six reviewers and the validator. The review was rebuilt statically: restore-set paths by comparing `.claude-pr/<path>` against the in-tree base copies, and other paths (scripts/, tests/, docs/, .env.example, .github/) from head content only. Provenance for findings outside the restore set is unverified.

Could not read the PR title, body, closing issues or comment threads (gh unavailable), so there was no steering brief and no spec-source detection; `review-spec` was not spawned. The second freshness assertion (HEAD vs headRefOid) could not run. The full head SHA could not be resolved, so the important finding's body carries no SHA permalink.

Size-gated instance scaling was skipped: correctness, security and maintainability ran as one instance each, since without the diff stat the gate couldn't be measured or split by subsystem. Maintainability ran on opus because the PR deletes ~30 skills, which is a large diff. One reviewer nit (plugin name `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official` unverifiable offline) was dropped as an unproven mechanism.
